chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qawlawayh, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, who reported from Sulaiman ibn Salemah al-Kindi, from Muhammad ibn Saeed ibn Ghazwan and Isa ibn Abu Mansur, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who reported that Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them, said:

A person who sighs in grief over the wrongs done to us, that sigh is glorification of Allah, and his anxiety about us is an act of worship, and to conceal our secrets is a struggle in the way of Allah. Then Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said: This hadith ought to be written in gold.

key_terms.جهاد في سبيل الله: Jihad fi sabil Allah: striving in the way of Allah

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq say about those who grieve for the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) declares three spiritual rewards for those who grieve over the oppression suffered by the Ahl al-Bayt: their sighs of sorrow are counted as glorification of Allah, their anxiety is considered worship, and guarding the secrets of the Imams is equivalent to jihad in the path of Allah. The Imam then emphasized the extraordinary importance of this tradition by saying it ought to be written in gold. This hadith was taught in the context of taqiyyah and the suffering of the Shia community under political persecution.
word_analysis: for the wrongs done to us
